title: Scaling Recurrence-aware Foundation Models for Clinical Records via Next-Visit Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2603.24562v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: While large-scale pretraining has revolutionized language modeling, its potential remains underexplored in healthcare with structured electronic health records (EHRs). We present RAVEN, a novel generative pretraining strategy for sequential EHR data based on Recurrence-Aware next-Visit EveNt prediction. Leveraging a dataset of over one million unique individuals, our model learns to autoregressively generate tokenized clinical events for the next visit conditioned on patient history. We introduce regularization on predicting repeated events and highlight a key pitfall in EHR-based foundation model evaluations: repeated event tokens can inflate performance metrics when new onsets are not distinguished from subsequent occurrences. Furthermore, we empirically investigate the scaling behaviors in a data-constrained, compute-saturated regime, showing that simply increasing model size is suboptimal without commensurate increases in data vo

translated_title: 通过下次就诊预测扩展具有复发感知能力的临床记录基础模型
translated_abstract: 尽管大规模预训练已经在语言建模领域引发了革命，但其在医疗保健领域（尤其是结构化电子健康记录EHR）的潜力仍未得到充分探索。我们提出了RAVEN，这是一种基于“复发感知的下次就诊事件预测”的针对序列化EHR数据的新型生成式预训练策略。利用包含超过一百万独立个体的数据集，我们的模型学会了以患者病史为条件，自回归地生成下次就诊的分词化临床事件。我们引入了对重复事件预测的正则化方法，并指出了基于EHR的基础模型评估中的一个关键陷阱：当新发事件与后续复发事件未被区分时，重复的事件token可能会虚高性能指标。此外，我们实证研究了在数据受限、计算资源趋于饱和情形下的缩放行为，结果表明，在没有相应增加数据量的情况下，单纯增大模型规模并非最优策略。
tldr: 本文提出RAVEN——一种基于复发感知的下次就诊事件预测的临床记录基础模型预训练策略，揭示了重复事件token虚高评估指标的陷阱，并证明在数据受限时单纯扩大模型规模并非最优。
en_tdlr: This paper presents RAVEN, a recurrence-aware next-visit event prediction pretraining strategy for clinical foundation models, exposing the pitfall of repeated event tokens inflating evaluation metrics and demonstrating that simply scaling up model size is suboptimal under data constraints.
